text:
devon: Quick kickoff 1: goal is to make the function/tool-calling docs linkable by slicing the long page into three tiny, copyable snippets: invoke, output-schema, parse-fallback. Keeps READMEs small and references stable.

ana: Agreed. Anchor ids we should use: snippet-invoke, snippet-output-schema, snippet-parse-fallback. Use kebab-case and no generated hashes.

rob: I'll split the big example and add those headings. My PR will only touch headings and code fences so it should be low risk.

maya: I'll take the JSON schema examples. Keep them minimal (required props only) and include one small shim example when the tool returns extras, e.g. `{
  "id": 42,
  "result": "OK",
  "meta": { "duration_ms": 120 }
}` then show schema that expects id+result only and a one-line shim: `const { id, result } = response;`.

devon: Also add a one-line parse fallback note under the fallback snippet: "Fallback order: strict JSON -> tolerant JSON -> regex fallback." Include a tiny CLI example showing strict parse fail then fallback.

ana: For SDK examples note differences by major: label 3.x vs 4.x. e.g. "SDK 3.x: client.invoke({ name: 'send_email', input })" and "SDK 4.x: client.tools.invoke('send_email', input)".

ci-bot: deploy-preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood/docs/invoke-slices-17495 (auto). CI lint passed. :white_check_mark:

rob: Timeline: please open small focused PRs by Friday EOD. Prefix with `docs: invoke snippets`. I'll open the split PR tomorrow.

maya: I'll have the schema PR by Thursday. Tag me when it's up.

devon: Thanks all. Keep snippets under ~20 lines and add copy buttons using <Snippet lang="ts" copy /> or <Snippet lang="py" copy /> where appropriate. Ping me for review. :thumbsup:
